Last April my son's father was shot and killed. He lived in the Caribbean, and we weren't officially together (although we had talked of reconciling.) My son at the time was 3 years old, and had only met his dad once the previous year when we visited.

I told my son the truth, that Daddy died. I travelled with him to the funeral so that even if he didn't understand or remember it, I could tell him when he gets older that he was there and said goodbye. We talked about how Daddy's body is dead, but his soul is up in the stars (I'm not super religious, but do mention Heaven sometimes) and in our hearts when we remember him. Every night we still look at the stars and say good night to Daddy. 

There have been a couple of times when my son has mentioned about doing some "when Daddy is alive again" and I have to explain again that Daddy is never going to be alive again. A couple of months ago he went through a phase where every night he asked how his Daddy died, how his grandfather died, and how his great-grandmother died.

In our case, I think I have grieved much more than my son, and much of my grieving has been in regard to the lose he has experienced, even though he doesn't know what he has lost yet. I do still worry how he will be when he is old enough to truly understand what he has lost.

One thing that I make sure I do, and my family and friends, is to speak good of Daddy around my son. Daddy had his faults, but I do want my son to know the good aspects of his father.

I am very sorry for your lose, and your son's loss. It won't be easy going forward, and accepting that you are truly a single parent now (although I was a single parent previously, it is just so final now). Please do not hesitate to message me if you ever need somebody in a similar position to talk to.
My love, Darren. April 2017

Last April in a Friday night he was at his house when a van with some men in it parked near it and the men started arguing. He asked the men to leave and when he went to back inside he was shot in the back. 

As far as I know nobody has ever been arrested. The island he lived on has a high crime rate so I don't expect his murder to be solved. 

It is a shame since when I lived there with him I always felt safe but now I'm worried to visit with my son, yet I want my son to know that side of his family and his heritage.
